result.rangeText: Working range {{min}}–{{max}} cm. Start here, adjust 1 cm from how the boat feels.

setup.title: Full setup for these conditions
setup.throatPeakText: Always as tight as possible, every day. The two most important ties on the boat.

light.sprit: A hint of the diagonal crease may remain, especially downwind — keep the leech soft.
light.luff: Slightly loose: about 5–10 mm gap between sail and mast for a rounder, more powerful entry.
light.outhaul: Eased — a hand's width of depth between boom and foot of the sail.
light.vang: Just snug or slightly slack so the leech stays open.
light.body: Weight well forward, by the mast thwart. Sit still — every movement shakes wind out of the sail.

lm.sprit: Tension until the throat-to-clew crease just disappears.
lm.luff: Moderate — sail close to the mast but not pinned.
lm.vang: Snug once sheeted in for upwind.
lm.body: Weight starting to move aft and out as pressure builds.

med.sprit: Crease just removed. If gusty, ease 1 cm so the peak can breathe.
med.luff: Snug — sail sitting close to the mast for a flatter entry.
med.vang: Firm. Set it sheeted in for upwind before the start.
med.board: Fully down upwind; halfway on reaches.
med.body: Hiking. In gusts: ease the sheet first, hike, steer up slightly — in that order.

fresh.sprit: Ease 1–2 cm from “crease just gone” upwind so the leech twists open and dumps the gusts. Re-tension a touch downwind.
fresh.luff: Tight — sail almost touching the mast.
fresh.outhaul: Tight, foot nearly flat along the boom.
fresh.vang: Firm — essential so the boom doesn't sky when she eases in a gust.
fresh.board: Raised 5–10 cm upwind to reduce trip force; well up downwind.
fresh.body: Full hiking, active mainsheet. Ease 20–30 cm the moment a gust hits, trim back as the boat flattens.

strong.sprit: Eased noticeably upwind — an open, twisted leech is the biggest depower left.
strong.vang: Firm — critical downwind to prevent a death roll.
strong.board: Up 10 cm upwind; most of the way up downwind.
strong.body: Survival mode is normal and fine at this weight. Flat boat, eased sheet, pick moments. Getting round the course is the win.

howTo.title: How to use the number
howTo.measuringText: hook a tape over the mast tip and measure to the top aft edge of the transom, on centerline. Figures assume a standard sail cut — your sailmaker's guide may sit 1–2 cm away, so treat this as a starting point.
howTo.onWaterText: hiking flat out and still heeling → rake 1 cm more next time. Boat feels dead → stand it up 1 cm. Change one thing at a time so she learns what each control does.

buyBoat.title: Buying an Optimist
buyBoat.subtitle: Guide to finding the right boat
buyBoat.description: Buying an Optimist is a big step. Here you'll find price guides and tips on what to look for — from beginner boats to race-ready dinghies.
buyBoat.priceBeginnerNote: Older boat for exploring the sport
buyBoat.priceRacingNote: Good condition for training and racing
buyBoat.priceCompNote: Serious competition at a high level
buyBoat.tip1: Buy an approved one-design boat (Winner, Finessa, Osis, OS, Nordest, etc.)
buyBoat.tip2: The hull (without block, lines or sail) must weigh at least 35 kg
buyBoat.tip3: Check that a measurement certificate is included — it is required
buyBoat.tip4: Good places to search: Blocket.se and jolleplan.se

harborSpots.title: Harbor Dinghy Spots
harborSpots.subtitle: Boat storage March–October
harborSpots.description: KKKK offers dinghy spots at the harbor during the sailing season. Spots come in two categories depending on location and crane access.
harborSpots.priceCraneNote: Includes free crane lift during season
harborSpots.tip1: Season runs March–October — boats must be removed by November 15
harborSpots.tip2: Boat must have a visible decal and wagon label for identification
harborSpots.tip3: Boats left unclaimed for over one year become club property

mastStorage.title: Mast Storage
mastStorage.subtitle: Included in training fees
mastStorage.description: Active Optimist sailors in a training group can store their rig, rudder and centerboard in the club's mast shed — free for those who have paid training fees.
mastStorage.tip1: Spot is included in training fees — no extra cost for active sailors
mastStorage.tip2: Administered by parent coordinators within the Optimist training group
mastStorage.tip3: Available spaces are posted inside the shed itself
mastStorage.tip4: Equipment must be removed when you stop attending training
